title: Federating application segments to a partner

prose.text: Only some application segments can be federated, and the guest sees them through a pair of fields.

prose.label: Segment fields.
prose.text: {{guest-details-shape}} {{python-guestdetails-decode-defect}} The meaning of the field and its three companions is open, see [[zpa.app-segments.api-fields:hbr-sticky-guest-semantics]]. The wider segment sharing model between Microtenants is a different feature: [[zpa.microtenants.share-and-move]].
Writing a populated Python PartnerInfo back has its own defect: {{python-partnerinfo-request-format-unset}}

checks.do: Whether the application segment uses IP addresses or has any of the six blocking settings enabled.
Whether a partner was deselected and saved, since guest end users then lose access immediately.
Whether guestDetails read through the Python SDK raises on a segment that is federated to a partner.
What hbrEnabled, stickyEntity, stickyGroup and guestDetails mean, which no source defines.

federate-flow.statement: On the Defined Application Segments page the host selects a segment's Federate Application icon, selects one or more partners to share with, and saves.

quotes: Locate the application segment you want to federate in the table, and then click the Federate Application icon ().
Partners: Select one or more partners to share applications with.

deselect-loses-access.statement: After a partner is deselected and the change saved, the end users on the guest partner side immediately lose access to all applications.

quotes: After deselecting the partner and saving, the end users from the guest partner side will immediately lose access to all applications.

no-ip-applications.statement: Applications using IP addresses cannot be federated because of potential IP address overlap and routing conflicts in the guest partner's network.

quotes: Applications using IP addresses (e.g., 192.168.1.10) cannot be federated due to potential IP address overlap and routing conflicts in the guest partner's network.

must-be-disabled.statement: To federate an application segment, Source IP Anchor, Double Encryption, Bypass, Bypass during Reauthentication, ZIA Inspection and AppProtection must be disabled on it.

evidence.after: the following application segment configurations must be disabled to federate an application segment:

guests-must-be-active-partners.statement: The federate operation's `guestGids` must be the partners that the host has an active federation with.

expect.description: The list of guest partner GIDs to share the application with. This array must be the partners that the host has an active federation with.

guest-details-shape.statement: In the Go SDK the base, Browser Access, Inspection and PRA application segment models carry `guestDetails`, where each guest record has a `federationId` and a `partnerInfo` with approval status, federation status, partner GID, name and scope name.

python-guestdetails-decode-defect.statement: The Python SDK's `GuestDetails` model builds a non-null `partnerInfo` with `common.PartnerInfo`, which the shared models module does not define, so decoding a segment with non-null `partnerInfo` raises an AttributeError; the model defines a local `PartnerInfo` class that it does not use.
python-guestdetails-decode-defect.conditions: Absence search at the pinned commit: `grep -n 'class PartnerInfo' zscaler/zpa/models/common.py` returns nothing, and the only PartnerInfo classes are in models/application_segment.py and models/tenant_federation_provisioning.py. The raise was inferred from the missing attribute and not run.

python-partnerinfo-request-format-unset.statement: In the Python SDK the PartnerInfo model's `request_format()` reads `self.partner_info`, but its constructor sets that attribute only when it is built without a config, so a populated PartnerInfo has no such attribute.

quotes:
